title: POC Weekly Security Sync - AquaCloud Bank
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on SSO integration progress, audit log sampling, data retention settings, and SOC 2 artifacts. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 kit and audit log sample; AquaCloud to provide SSO metadata and confirm retention policy for pilot; schedule latency/cost bench with dedicated capacity next week.
topics: SSO / SAML metadata and IdP config
Audit logs and access logging format
Data retention and masking during pilot
next_steps: Redwood: send SOC2 summary + compliance pack (link) by 2026-04-09
Customer: share SAML metadata and test user by 2026-04-10
Redwood: provide sample audit log export and field mapping by 2026-04-09
Schedule bench for dedicated capacity w/ Diego (week of 2026-04-13)
action_items: Maya Chen - Send SOC2 summary + redacted controls matrix - due 2026-04-09
Diego Ramos - Prepare sample audit log export (JSON) and mapping doc - due 2026-04-09
Priya Patel - Provide SAML IdP metadata and test account - due 2026-04-10
Markus Voss - Confirm pilot data retention policy and masking rules - due 2026-04-10
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'll run through the agenda -- SSO, audit logs, retention, SOC 2 artifacts, then quick bench plan.
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good, Maya. We only have 45 minutes so we'll keep it tight.
[00:15] Diego Ramos: Quick intro from our side, Diego from Redwood infra, I'll be the SE on the bench and log exports.
[00:20] Markus Voss: Markus here, we'll be the cloud lead for the pilot.
[00:24] Priya Patel: Priya, security engineering, handling SSO and data retention.
[00:28] Maya Chen: Great. First item SSO. Priya I think you uploaded a note to the workspace but I don't see the metadata yet?
[00:35] Priya Patel: Right, I started the metadata, we tried the basic SAML flow yesterday but got a cert mismatch error. The redirect URI looked fine, but the cert thumbprint on Redwood side didn't match our IdP export. Could be encoding, sometimes the cert gets extra headers in the XML.
[00:50] Diego Ramos: Ah yeah, we've seen that when the IdP exports the cert with line breaks or when the xml has BOM. We have a helper script we usually share, I'll attach that. The flow we recommend: get the metadata XML, strip non-ASCII chars, confirm sha1 thumbprint, then upload via Console.
[01:10] Lena Ortiz: For compliance we need SSO SAML with SCIM provisioning ideally. Is SCIM available in pilot?
[01:18] Maya Chen: SCIM is in Dedicated and Private modes; for Hosted we support provisioning through a limited SCIM endpoint during pilots. Diego, correct me if I'm wrong on the exact endpoints we provide in the POC.
[01:26] Diego Ramos: For pilot we can spin up a time-limited SCIM endpoint with token auth. It's not the full enterprise SCIM service, but it supports create/update/delete for pilot users. Recommend using it for test users only.
[01:38] Priya Patel: That works as long as tokens are rotated and logged.
[01:42] Diego Ramos: Yes, token rotation is available in Console; we can also provide a short-lived token.
[01:47] Maya Chen: Action: Priya to share IdP metadata and a test user by Friday. (notes: Priya agrees)
[01:52] Priya Patel: I'll do that.
[01:54] Maya Chen: Next - audit logs. Diego, you were going to show an example of what Redwood exports look like?
[02:00] Diego Ramos: Yep, I have a sample prepared. The export is JSON lines (ndjson) with fields: timestamp, request_id, user_id, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, status, host_region, and an obfuscated prompt hash. For pilot we can include more or fewer fields.
[02:18] Markus Voss: Can we also log the calling IP and VPC info? For our auditors it's important to show network origin.
[02:24] Diego Ramos: We capture source_ip and region; for VPC we include a vpc_id field when deployed to Private or Dedicated in the customer's VPC. For Hosted there's an internal routing tag, but not your private VPC id.
[02:36] Lena Ortiz: We need to ensure logs are tamper-evident and we can pull a signed digest for a date range - do you provide something like that?
[02:44] Diego Ramos: We can provide a signed checksum of exports, yes. We generally sign daily export bundles with an HMAC using a Redwood key; if you run Dedicated or Private you can swap in your KMS to sign on your side.
[02:58] Priya Patel: For the pilot, can you include consistent user mapping so we can correlate with our SSO ids?
[03:05] Diego Ramos: Yes, the user_id in logs is the Redwood account id; we can also include an external_subject field which is the SAML NameID or SCIM id if you enable it. We'll include a mapping doc.
[03:16] Maya Chen: Action: Diego to share sample audit log ndjson and mapping doc by Thursday.
[03:22] Diego Ramos: Noted. I'll include a small sample (last 24 hours) with synthetic events so you can validate parsers.
[03:28] Lena Ortiz: Data retention. For the pilot we want a 30-day window and then automatic deletion; masked prompts must be retained only for 7 days. Is that doable?
[03:37] Diego Ramos: We support configurable retention on a per-bucket basis for Dedicated/Private. On Hosted we have retention tiers; for a pilot we can set short-term retention to 30 days and a separate prompt retention to 7 days with optional prompt hashing instead of storing raw prompts.
[03:51] Priya Patel: Clarify: prompt hashing - is it reversible? Our policy forbids reversible storage of PII.
[03:58] Diego Ramos: The prompt hashing we provide is one-way SHA-256 with salt; we don't keep mapping to original. For additional safety we can apply token-level masking on the service to redact known PII patterns before logging. It's heuristic but works for many pilots.
[04:12] Markus Voss: For regulated flows we might want to run on Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
[04:17] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated gives you customer KMS integration and full VPC network isolation; it also gives more control over logs and signing. We'll outline delta vs Hosted in the SOC2 pack.
[04:28] Lena Ortiz: Speaking of SOC 2, where are we on evidence? We need an SOC 2 report and ideally a controls matrix that maps our requirements to Redwood controls.
[04:36] Maya Chen: We have a SOC 2 Type II report; I can send a redacted copy and a controls matrix that maps to typical banking controls. I will mark any items that require Dedicated deployment for full compliance.
[04:48] Priya Patel: We need to know which controls are in-scope for Hosted vs Dedicated. Also encryption at rest key ownership - clarify who holds keys.
[04:57] Diego Ramos: Hosted: Redwood KMS with customer-managed envelope keys via external KMS for certain fields; Dedicated/Private: you can bring your own KMS/HSM, full key control. I'll put a short table in the pack.
[05:12] Lena Ortiz: Audit log retention and deletion proofs will be part of our audit checklist. Will you provide deletion receipts or logs?
[05:20] Diego Ramos: We can include deletion events in the audit log stream and provide a signed deletion manifest for the deleted objects.
[05:28] Maya Chen: We'll add that to the sample audit export doc.
[05:32] Priya Patel: Regarding legal review - we have to check data residency during pilot. Some test data will be EU-only. Is your Hosted region in eu-west-1 available for the pilot?
[05:40] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Hosted has eu-west-1 region; we can pin the pilot to eu-west to keep data resident there. For Dedicated/Private you can choose region too.
[05:48] Markus Voss: Ok good. Bench plan: Diego, you said you'd run a small smoke test with the Dedicated config to capture latency and token costs so we can sign off?
[05:58] Diego Ramos: Correct. Plan: run a 1-hour smoke with a small set of prompts (1000 requests, mixed lengths), measure p50/p95 latency, tokens in/out, and cost per 1k tokens. For Dedicated we'll test with the same model but pinned instance types to show predictable throughput.
[06:15] Lena Ortiz: We'll need the bench results for the security review board next week. Can you have a raw CSV and a short write-up?
[06:22] Diego Ramos: Yes, I'll produce CSV + a 1-page summary.
[06:26] Maya Chen: Action: Schedule bench week of 2026-04-13. Diego to propose slots.
[06:32] Priya Patel: One more question: entitlements and RBAC - we want to limit production model changes to specific roles and have view-only for security. Is that supported?
[06:41] Diego Ramos: RBAC is available; roles include admin, deployer, reader, auditor. You can integrate with SAML groups for mapping. We'll share the RBAC matrix.
[06:50] Lena Ortiz: Great. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[06:53] Maya Chen: Nothing major. We'll send the SOC 2 pack and the logs sample; Diego will prepare the bench script and log export.
[07:02] Priya Patel: From our side the only blocker is getting the SAML metadata and a test account. We'll try to get that by Friday.
[07:09] Maya Chen: Recap and next steps - I'll summarize and send notes.
[07:12] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send SOC 2 summary and controls matrix, Diego to send sample audit log ndjson + mapping, schedule bench for week of 4/13, customer to share SAML metadata and confirm retention policy.
[07:24] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all.
[07:26] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the doc.
[07:30] -- meeting ends --

Notes: occasional transcript artifacts: some vendor names mis-heard as "SaturnServe" in the transcript. Links referenced: Redwood SOC2 pack (link provided in follow-up), sample audit log (s3 link shared in an email), bench script (internal).
